trial_court: Additional Family Court-I, East Singhbhum at Jamshedpur (Original Suit No. 314 of 2016)
case_name: Vijay Kumar vs Smt. Sagarika Devi
facts_of_case: Marriage between Vijay Kumar and Sagarika Devi was solemnized in 2007. After marriage, the respondent-wife came to reside with the petitioner-husband for a period of 15 days. The respondent's behavior during this time was abnormal, and she was unable to perform household chores or understand family matters.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the other spouse has been suffering from incurable mental disease.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant-husband that the Learned Family Court below has failed to appreciate that the petitioner /appellant has produced credible evidence which are sufficient to establish that the respondent-wife has been suffering from menta retardation and therefore the petitioner /appellant is entitled for grant of decree of divorce.
use_in: cases involving divorce on grounds of incurable mental disease

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must substantiate their claim with credible evidence.
legal_principles.held: Submission has also been made that the learned Court below also failed to appreciate that the petitioner /appellant has successfully substantiated that the decree of Judicial separation between the petitioner and the respondent has been passed on 04.04.2013 in Mat. Suit No. 52 of 2011, wherein it was ordered that if cohabitation takes place between the petitioner and the respondent for a period of one year, the petitioner shall be at liberty to file a case for divorce.
use_in: cases involving divorce on grounds of judicial separation

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision dismissing the petition for divorce was upheld by the High Court.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
